correctness.rationale: Nonresonant box-section vertices have exactly one unsaturated coordinate; an exchange proof makes the Gaussian optimum a sorted capacity-filling permutation. Counting exactly |H|!(n-|H|-1)! braid chambers gives normal-cone angles; uniform subset prefixes give exact rank tails. Reversal gives symmetry, all n<=4 laws follow from presence or absence of a dominant weight, and a pairwise-intersecting winning-edge graph bounds h<=4 for n5. Five witnesses and a sixth dominant profile attain all classes. Exact prefix sums establish majorization and direct convexity gives the strict reverse convex order for the n5 counterexample. CHECK.py independently replayed 520 finite generic profiles and 750 direct objective maximizations; universality is proved analytically.

originality.rationale: Ferroni–McGinnis introduces this geometric family and its Ehrhart/weighted-permutation enumerations, not the Gaussian angular first-majorization boundary. Castillo–Liu describes general braid-fan coarsening, but not this exact six-class pivotal-position distribution or majorization reversal. The classical Shapley–Shubik framework identifies the same pivotal mechanism and is expressly not claimed as new; the sharp five-coordinate convex-order reversal and complete rank-law classification were not located in inspected sources or related indexed scientific records. Voting-literature equivalence remains a meaningful residual risk.
residual_risks: Shapley–Shubik (1954) primary full paper was not available on the accessible publisher page; its classical pivot correspondence is fully credited, but an unseen position-distribution discussion cannot be categorically excluded.
Large and partly unindexed weighted-voting pivotal-position literature could contain the sharp five-coordinate majorization comparison under another name.
Closest public mathematical-record hits were available as indexed summaries rather than complete files, limiting global coverage claims; no decisive covering theorem was identified.

value.rationale: The statistic is a canonical solid-angle distribution of exposed vertices of a natural family of generalized permutohedra, with a precise random-direction sampling interpretation. The result classifies ALL six generic five-coordinate rank laws, identifies the first ambient dimension at which capacity balancing can increase rather than decrease angular rank dispersion, and supplies an exact example that reverses the entire convex-order comparison, not just one plotted moment. These are motivated structural geometric facts with finite-dimension sharpness, though they do not assert a general large-dimensional law.
